venues.name: Antonio 劉老師小提琴STUDIO 琴行

blurb.long: It took Yeung Koon-yat 3 years to learn how to cook abalone, and the method he settled on is still why people book Forum. Dried Japanese abalone goes into a clay pot on a bed of bamboo shoots and spare ribs, with chicken on top, and braises for 12 to 14 hours. The dish carries his name: Ah Yat's abalone. He cooked it for Deng Xiaoping in 1984 and for Jacques Chirac in 1995. Yeung died in 2023, at 90. Chef Adam Wong, at Forum for more than 30 years and named as his culinary heir, keeps the Cantonese classics on the menu, and the dining room has barely changed. It holds 3 Michelin stars. Order the abalone, then the Ah Yat fried rice, which has a following of its own.
blurb.short: Yeung Koon-yat, Hong Kong's "abalone king," made Forum famous with abalone braised for 12 to 14 hours. It's still the dish to order at this three-star Causeway Bay classic.
